_comment: Documented false negatives of the selection: major political figures the fame metric (English Wikipedia pageviews + language editions) under-ranks, mostly national icons of the French-speaking launch market, or that the Wikidata category queries / occupation filter miss. They are always selected (taking the place of the lowest merit picks, never of continent-quota picks) and override exclusions; their rarity is still assigned purely by fame rank. Keep this list short and justified.

Q2038.name: François Mitterrand
Q2038.reason: President of France 1981–1995; under-ranked by English pageviews.

Q171730.name: Georges Clemenceau
Q171730.reason: French Prime Minister who led France to victory in 1918.

Q298180.name: Simone Veil
Q298180.reason: Minister who legalised abortion in France, first elected President of the European Parliament.

Q12688.name: Jean Jaurès
Q12688.reason: Founder of French socialism, assassinated in 1914.

Q26702.name: Cardinal de Richelieu
Q26702.reason: Chief minister of Louis XIII, architect of the absolutist French state.

Q184623.name: Georges Danton
Q184623.reason: Leading figure of the French Revolution.

Q186652.name: Lafayette
Q186652.reason: Hero of the American and French revolutions.

Q7226.name: Joan of Arc
Q7226.reason: War leader of the Hundred Years' War; no political office, so the category queries miss her.

Q182276.name: Benito Juárez
Q182276.reason: President of Mexico, symbol of the Reform.

Q17410.name: Zhou Enlai
Q17410.reason: First Premier of the People's Republic of China.

Q2492.name: Konrad Adenauer
Q2492.reason: First Chancellor of West Germany, founder of European integration.

Q40933.name: Eva Perón
Q40933.reason: First Lady and political leader of Argentina; the actor occupation wrongly excludes her.

Q269909.name: Andy Burnham
Q269909.reason: Sitting Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (since July 2026); too recent for the long pageview window.
